findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext values. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance (and is stored unencrypted), leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance's root volume is created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with a publicly reachable web server, this makes SSRF-based theft of instance metadata (including the credentials in user data) considerably easier.

The instance is placed in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and attached to a security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 22 and 80, so it is directly reachable from the internet including for SSH administration.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 (cleartext HTTP with no TLS alternative), and egress permits all protocols and ports to any destination, which facilitates data exfiltration and command-and-control from a compromised host.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true, so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken of an unencrypted volume and no encryption/KMS key is specified, so the snapshot copy of the data is stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and public access block
findings.description: The VPC flow log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, no public access block, no versioning, and no policy restricting access, leaving sensitive network telemetry unencrypted at rest and at risk of accidental public exposure.
No bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is attached, allowing flow log data to be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the network boundary and directly exposing workloads to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the network boundary and directly exposing workloads to the internet.

The VPC's default security group is not restricted with an aws_default_security_group resource, so any resource inadvertently placed in it inherits AWS default allow-all intra-group traffic rather than an explicitly denied posture.
